name: dilute concentration held by droplets that divide (control)
question: Does the dilute concentration of a droplet-forming species return to its set point after a step of its supply, and through which variable?

provenance.source: droplet growth by Gibbs-Thomson exchange with the dilute phase: I. M. Lifshitz and V. V. Slyozov, J. Phys. Chem. Solids 19, 35 (1961); C. Wagner, Z. Elektrochem. 65, 581 (1961); turnover of the droplet material inside the droplets: D. Zwicker, A. A. Hyman and F. Juelicher, Phys. Rev. E 92, 012317 (2015); mean field for identical droplets; division of active droplets above a critical size: D. Zwicker, R. Seyboldt, C. A. Weber, A. A. Hyman and F. Juelicher, Nat. Phys. 13, 408 (2017)

assumptions: dimensionless: u = c/c_sat, r = R/R0, time in rho R0^2/(D c_sat), j the supply, kappa1 the removal in the dilute phase, kappa2 the turnover inside the droplets, Gamma = 4 pi n R0^3 rho/c_sat, eps the capillary length over R0
droplets divide at a rate proportional to the excess of their radius over r_div, conserving the dense volume n r^3 (continuum form of division at a critical size)
n is the number of droplets relative to its reference value; kdiv = 1, r_div = 1.8
values kappa1 = 0.06, Gamma = 1, eps = 0.001, kappa2 = 0.03 (chosen; droplets above the ripening radius (3 eps/(2 kappa2))^(1/3) = 0.37)
the step of the input: the supply j from 0.12 to 0.18 and 0.24 (2 to 4 kappa1)
observable: dilute concentration u relative to saturation

regulation.change: droplets divide above r_div, so their number follows the supply at fixed size
